1.explanation:
1. revealMetadataFilter (metadata.ts) is responsible for taking the user’s kebab-cased options (including hash-type) and converting them into the camelCase properties the rest of the code expects. If hash-type isn’t correctly filtered and passed through, the downstream code that handles centering the title slide won’t see the setting.
2. revealjsFormat (format-reveal.ts) picks up the hashType setting and translates it into the appropriate Reveal.js configuration. The comment “hash-type: number (as shorthand for –auto_identifiers)” lives here, so any logic around enabling numeric slide IDs lives in this function.
3. revealHtmlPostprocessor (format-reveal.ts) applies post‐render fixes on each <section> element. In particular it contains the comment “if we are using ’number’ as our hash type then remove the title slide id” and also handles adding the CSS class that centers the title slide. If the ID is removed (or never recognized because the hashType value wasn’t passed through correctly), the centering selector never matches and the title slide is left-aligned.

To fix the bug, the flow of the hash-type setting must be restored: revealMetadataFilter must include the kHashType key so that revealjsFormat sees it, and revealHtmlPostprocessor must not strip or mis‐apply the slide ID/class that triggers the centering style when hashType is “number.”
1.bug_scenario: The two screenshots show the title slide rendered by the Reveal.js format under Quarto with different “hash-type” settings. In the first (working) case, where hash-type: title is used, the title, subtitle, author and date are all centered as expected. In the second (broken) case, with hash-type: number, the title block has been shifted to the upper left (and the usual centering CSS never applies), leaving the slide misaligned.

2.explanation:
• revealMetadataFilter (metadata.ts): This function normalizes kebab-cased metadata into camelCase Reveal.js options. It does not special-case the custom `hash-type` setting, so downstream code never sees the numeric-hash directive.

• revealjsFormat (format-reveal.ts): The stubbed comment "// hash-type: number (as shorthand for -auto_identifiers)" indicates where `hash-type` should be translated into Reveal.js’s `hash` and `hashOneBasedIndex` settings—but no implementation appears to be present to do so, so `hash-type` is effectively ignored or mishandled.

• revealHtmlPostprocessor (format-reveal.ts): This postprocessor contains the logic to remove the title‐slide ID when `hash-type: number` is detected, but it does not reapply centering (or adjust the `center` configuration) on the stripped slide. As a result, the title slide loses both its ID anchor and its centering class when numeric hashes are enabled.

Together, these functions constitute the metadata handling, format construction, and post-processing stages that should interpret `hash-type: number`, remove the title‐slide ID, and then restore centering. Fixing the bug will require augmenting revealMetadataFilter to recognize `hash-type`, implementing the translation in revealjsFormat, and ensuring revealHtmlPostprocessor reapplies centering to the title slide.
2.bug_scenario: The two screenshots illustrate the title‐slide centering behavior when using Quarto’s Reveal.js output with different hash-type settings. In the first (working) image, using `hash-type: title` the slide’s title, subtitle and author/date block are centered on the page. In the second (broken) image, using `hash-type: number` the metadata block is stripped of its default ID and the title slide is no longer auto‐centered: all text shifts to the left, and the date anchors at the bottom left.
